questions.q: If $a, b$ and $c$ be three distinct real numbers in G.P. and $a + b + c = xb,$ then $x$ cannot be:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given $a, b, c$ are in G.P.

Let common ratio of G.P. be $r$ , then $b = ar, c = a{r}^{2}$

Given equation can be written as

$a + ar + a{r}^{2} = x . a . r$

$⇒ x = r + \dfrac{1}{r} + 1$

As we know $r > 0,$ then $r + \dfrac{1}{r} \ge 2 ⇒ x \ge 3$

$r < 0,$ then $r + \dfrac{1}{r} \le - 2 ⇒ x \le - 1$

$⇒ x \in \left(- \infty, - 1\right] ∪ \left[3, \infty\right)$

Hence, $x \ne 2 .$

questions.q: If $n$~arithmetic means are inserted between a and~$100$ such that the ratio of the first mean to the last mean is $1: 7$~and $a + n = 33$, then the value of~$n$ is

questions.solution:
Let the A.P. be& $a, {A}_{1}, {A}_{2} . . . {A}_{n}, 100$

Here, common difference,~$d = \dfrac{100 - a}{n + 1}$

Given~$\dfrac{A1}{An} = \dfrac{1}{7} ⇒ \dfrac{a + d}{100 - d} = \dfrac{1}{7} . . . \left(i\right)$

Also~$a + n = 33$

From options, when~$n = 23$,~$a = 10\text{and}d = $\dfrac{90}{24} = \dfrac{15}{4}

from~ \left(i\right)$~$\dfrac{10 + \dfrac{15}{4}}{100 - \dfrac{15}{4}} = \dfrac{55}{385} = \dfrac{1}{7}$

$

questions.q: $\text { If } x=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(-1)^n \tan ^{2n} \theta \text { and } y=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \cos ^{2 n} \theta \text {, for } 0\lt \theta\lt \frac{\pi}{4} \text {, then: }$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$y = 1 + \cos^{2} ⁡ \theta + \cos^{4} ⁡ \theta + \ldots$~ ~

Above series is an infinite G.P, apply sum of infinite G.P.

$⇒ y = \dfrac{1}{1 - \cos^{2} ⁡ \theta}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{y} = \sin^{2}\theta$

$x = \dfrac{1}{1 - \left(- \tan^{2} ⁡ \theta\right)} = \dfrac{1}{\sec^{2} ⁡ \theta}$

$⇒ \cos^{2} ⁡ \theta = x$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{y} + x = 1$

$⇒ y\left(1 - x\right) = 1$

questions.q: If $sin^{4}\alpha + 4cos^{4}\beta + 2 = 4\sqrt{2}sin\alphacos\beta$, $\alpha, \beta \in \left[$0, $\pi\right],~then $cos \left(\alpha + \beta\right) -cos \left(\alpha - \beta\right)is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$

We have,

$\sin^{4}\alpha + 4\cos^{4}\beta + 2 = 4\sqrt{2}sin\alphacos\beta$

Applying $AM \ge GM$, we get

\left(\dfrac{\sin^{4}\alpha + 4\cos^{4}\beta + 1 + 1}{4}\right) \ge \left(4sin^{4}\alpha \cdot cos^{4}\beta \cdot 1 \cdot 1\right)\dfrac{1}{4}$

$⇒ \sin^{4}\alpha + 4\cos^{4}\beta + 2 \ge 8sin\alphacos\beta$

And,~$AM = GM ⇒$numbers are equal and positive

$⇒ \sin^{4}\alpha = 4\cos^{4}\beta = 1$

$∴ sin^{4}\alpha = 1 ⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{π}{2}$~and

$cos\beta = \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ \beta = \dfrac{π}{4}$

Hence,

$cos \left(\alpha + \beta\right) -cos \left(\alpha - \beta\right)

$= - 2sin\$alphasin\beta

$= - 2 \times1 $\times $\dfrac{1}{2} = - \sqrt{2}$

$

questions.q: Let $a_1, a_2, a_3 \ldots$ be in an A.P. such that $\sum_{\mathrm{k}=1}^{12} \mathrm{a}_{2 \mathrm{k}-1}=-\frac{72}{5} \mathrm{a}_1, \mathrm{a}_1 \neq 0$. If $\sum_{\mathrm{k}=1}^{\mathrm{n}} \mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{k}}=0$, then n is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let $a_1=a$, common difference $=d$
$a_1+a_3+a_5+\ldots \ldots+a_{23}=-\frac{72}{5} a$
$\frac{12}{2}[2 a+11 \times 2 d]=-\frac{72}{5} a$
$12 a+132 d=-\frac{72}{5} a$
$132 a+132 \times 5 d=0$
$\mathrm{a}=-5 \mathrm{~d}$
$\frac{\mathrm{n}}{2}(2 \mathrm{a}+(\mathrm{n}-1) \mathrm{d})=0 \Rightarrow-10 \mathrm{~d}+\mathrm{nd}-\mathrm{d}=0$
$\mathrm{n}=11$

questions.q: Let $3, a, b, c$ be in $A . P .$ and $3, a - 1, b + 1, c + 9$ be in $G . P .$ Then, the arithmetic mean of $a, b$ and $c$ is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given: $3, a, b, c$ are in $A . P$

So, the common difference will be $d = a - 3$

Now, $b = 2a - 3$ and $c = 3a - 6$

Also, $3, a - 1, b + 1, c + 9$ are in $G . P$

So, $3 \left(c + 9\right) = \left($b + 1\right)\left($a - 1\right)$

$⇒ 3 \left($3a - 6 + 9\right) = \left(2a - 3 + 1\right)\left(a - 1\right)$

$⇒ 3 \left(3a + 3\right) = \left($2a - 2\$right)\left($a - 1\right)$

$⇒ 9a + 9 = 2a^{2} - 4a + 2$

$⇒ 2a^{2} - 13a - 7 = 0$

$⇒ a = 7, $\dfrac{- 1}{2} \left$\${\text{rejected}\right\}

So, $b = 2 \times7 - 3 = 11 & c = 3 \times7 - 6 = 15$

Now, the $A . M$ of $a, b, c$ is given by,

$⇒ A = \dfrac{a + b + c}{3}$

$⇒ A = \dfrac{7 + 11 + 15}{3}$

$⇒ A = \dfrac{33}{3}$

$⇒ A = 11

$

questions.q: Let ${A}_{1}$ and ${A}_{2}$ be two arithmetic means and ${G}_{1}, {G}_{2}$ and ${G}_{3}$ be three geometric means of two distinct positive numbers. Then~${G}_{1}^{4} + {G}_{2}^{4} + {G}_{3}^{4} + {G}_{1}^{2}{G}_{3}^{2}$& is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let the two numbers are $a, b$

$⇒ a, {A}_{1}, {A}_{2}, b$~are in AP.

$⇒ b = a + \left(4 - 1\right)d$

$⇒ d = \dfrac{b - a}{3}$

$⇒ {A}_{1} = a + \dfrac{b - a}{3} = \dfrac{2a + b}{3}$

$⇒ {A}_{2} = a + \dfrac{b - a}{3} \cdot 2 = \dfrac{a + 2b}{3}$

Similarly~$a, {G}_{1}, {G}_{2}, {G}_{3}, b$~are in GP.

$⇒ b = a\left(r\right)5 - 1$

$⇒ r = \left(\dfrac{b}{a}\right)\dfrac{1}{4}$

$⇒ {G}_{1} = a\left(\dfrac{b}{a}\right)\dfrac{1}{4}$

$⇒ {G}_{2} = a\left(\dfrac{b}{a}\right)\dfrac{2}{4}$

$⇒ {G}_{3} = a\left(\dfrac{b}{a}\right)\dfrac{3}{4}$

$= \left({G}_{1}\right)4 + \left({G}_{2}\right)4 + \left({G}_{3}\right)4 + \left({G}_{1}\right)2 \cdot \left({G}_{3}\right)2$

$⇒ a^{4} \cdot \dfrac{b}{a} + a^{4} \cdot \dfrac{b2}{a2} + a^{4} \cdot \dfrac{b3}{a3} + a^{4} \cdot \dfrac{b2}{a2}$

$= ba^{3} + b^{2}a^{2} + b^{3}a + a^{2}b^{2}$

$= ab\left(a^{2} + b^{2} + 2ab\right) = ab\left(a + b\right)2$

$⇒ \left({A}_{1} + {A}_{2}\right)2 \cdot {G}_{1}{G}_{3} = \left(a + b\right)2 \cdot ab$

Hence this is the correct option.

questions.q: Let $a, b, c, d\text{and}p$~be~non-zero distinct real numbers such that \left(a^{2} + b^{2} + c^{2}\right)p^{2} - 2 ( ab + bc + cd ) p + \left(b^{2} + c^{2} + d^{2}\right) = 0$. \text{ and } Then$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Rearranging the expression, we get
$( ap - b{)}^{2} + ( bp - c{)}^{2} + ( cp - d{)}^{2} = 0$
$\begin{cases}⇒ & ap - b = 0, bp - c = 0, cp - d = 0\end{cases}$

$\begin{cases}⇒ & p = \dfrac{b}{a} = \dfrac{c}{b} = \dfrac{d}{c}\end{cases}$

Which is condition of GP.

questions.q: If the minimum value of $f\left(x\right) = \dfrac{5x^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{α}{x5}, x > 0$, is $14$, then the value of $\alpha$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
From weighted $A . M . - G . M .$ inequality, we know

$\dfrac{5\left(\dfrac{x2}{2}\right) + 2\left(\dfrac{α}{2x^{5}}\right)}{5 + 2} \ge \left(\left(\dfrac{x2}{2}\right)5 \cdot \left(\dfrac{α}{2x^{5}}\right)2\right)\dfrac{1}{7}$

$⇒ \dfrac{5x^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{α}{x5} \ge \dfrac{7}{2}\left(\alpha\right)\dfrac{2}{7}$

Given that the least value of $\dfrac{5x^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{α}{x5}\text{is}14$

i.e.~$\dfrac{7}{2}\left(\alpha\right)\dfrac{2}{7} = 14 ⇒ \left(\alpha\right)\dfrac{1}{7} = 2 ⇒ \alpha = 128$

questions.q: Suppose that the number of terms in an A.P. is $2 k, k \in N$. If the sum of all odd terms of the A.P. is 40 , the sum of all even terms is 55 and the last term of the A.P. exceeds the first term by 27, then k is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let the A.P. be
$\begin{aligned}
& a, a+2, a+2 d, \ldots, a+(2 k-1) d \\
& \text { Now, } a+a+2 d+a+4 d+\ldots+a+(2 k-2) d=40 \\
& k a+2 d+4 d+\ldots+(2 k-2) d=40 \\
& \Rightarrow k a+\frac{k-1}{2}[2 d+2 k d-2 d]=40
\end{aligned}\Rightarrow k a+k(k-1) d=40$ ...(1)
And $a+d+a+3 d+\ldots+a+(2 k-1) d=55\Rightarrow k a+\frac{k}{2}(d+2 k d-d)=55\Rightarrow k a+k^2 d=55$ ....(2)
Also, $a+(2 k-1) d-a=27\Rightarrow \quad(2 k-1) d=27 \Rightarrow d=\frac{27}{2 k-1}$ ...(3)
From equation (1) and (2)
$k^2 d-k d-k^2 d=-15\Rightarrow \quad d=\frac{15}{k}$
From equation (3) and (4)
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{27}{2 k-1}=\frac{15}{k} \\
& 27 k=30 k-15 \\
& \Rightarrow 3 k=15 \\
& \Rightarrow k=5
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Three numbers are in an increasing geometric progression with common ratio $r .$~If the middle number is doubled, then the new numbers are in an arithmetic progression with common difference $d .$~If the fourth term of GP is $3r^{2},$~then $r^{2} - d$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
f$ax^{2} + bx + c = 0 ⇒ x = \dfrac{- b \pm \sqrt{b^{2} - 4ac}}{2ac}$

$⇒ r = \dfrac{4 \pm \sqrt{12}}{2} = 2 + \sqrt{3}, 2 - \sqrt{3}$

But it is an increasing~$G . P$

$∴ r = 2 + \sqrt{3}$

Given that Fourth~term of $G . P ⇒ {t}_{4} = ar^{2} = 3r^{2}$

$⇒ a = 3 .$

Common difference of an~$A . P = d = {t}_{2} - {t}_{1}$

$d = 2a - \dfrac{a}{r} = a \left(2 - \dfrac{1}{r}\right) =3 \left($2 - $\dfrac{1}{2 + \sqrt{3}}\right)

$= 3 ( 2 - 2 + $\sqrt{3} ) =3\sqrt{3}
Hence $r^{2} - d = ( 2 + $\sqrt{3}{)}^{2} - (3\sqrt{3} )

$= 4 + 3 + $4\sqrt{3} -3\sqrt{3}

$= 7 + $\sqrt{3}

$

questions.q: Consider two G.Ps. $2, {2}^{2}, {2}^{3}, \ldots$~and $4, {4}^{2}, {4}^{3}, \ldots$~of $60$~and $n$ terms respectively. If the geometric mean of all the $60 + n$~terms is  \left(2\right)\dfrac{225}{8}$, then $\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n}k\left(n - k\right)$& is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given two G.Ps. $2, {2}^{2}, {2}^{3}, \ldots$~and $4, {4}^{2}, {4}^{3}, \ldots$~of $60$~and $n$ terms respectively,

Also given~the geometric mean of all the $60 + n$~terms is \left(2\right)\dfrac{225}{8}$,

So,~\left(\left({2}^{1}{2}^{2} \ldots . {2}^{60}\right)\left({4}^{1} \cdot {4}^{2} \ldots \ldots . {4}^{n}\right)\right)\dfrac{1}{60 + n} = 2\dfrac{225}{8}$

$⇒ \left({2}^{30 \times 61}4\dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)}{2}\right)\dfrac{1}{60 + n} = 2\dfrac{225}{8}$

$⇒ {2}^{1830 + n^{2} + n} = 2\dfrac{\left(225\right)\left(60 + n\right)}{8}$

On comparing both side we get,

$⇒ 1830 + n^{2} + n = \dfrac{225\left(60 + n\right)}{8}$

$⇒ 8n^{2} - 217n + 1140 = 0$

$⇒ n = 20, \dfrac{57}{8}$

Now~$\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n}k\left(n - k\right) =\mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{20}nk - k^{2} = \dfrac{n^{2}\left(n + 1\right)}{2} - \dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)\left(2n + 1\right)}{6}$

$= \dfrac{{20}^{2} \times 21}{2} - \dfrac{20 \times 21 \times 41}{6} = 1330$

questions.q: The sum of an infinite geometric series with positive terms is 3 and the sum of the cubes of its terms is $\frac{27}{19}$. Then the common ratio of this series is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: Let the terms of infinite series are $a, a r, a r^{2}, a r^{3}, \ldots$ So, $\quad \frac{a}{1-r}=3$ Since, sum of cubes of its terms is $\frac{27}{19}$ that is sum of $a^{3}$, $a^{3} r^{3}, \ldots \infty$ is $\frac{27}{19}$ So, $\frac{a^{3}}{1-r^{3}}=\frac{27}{19}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{a}{1-r} \times \frac{a^{2}}{\left(1+r^{2}+r\right)}=\frac{27}{19}\Rightarrow \frac{9\left(1+r^{2}-2 r\right) \times 3}{1+r^{2}+r}=\frac{27}{19}\Rightarrow \quad 6 r^{2}-13 r+6=0\Rightarrow(3 r-2)(2 r-3)=0\Rightarrow r=\frac{2}{3},$ or $\frac{3}{2}$ As $|r| \lt 1$ So, $r=\frac{2}{3}$

questions.q: Let $x, y$ be positive real numbers and $m, n$ positive integers. The maximum value of the expression $\frac{x^{\mathrm{m}} y^{\mathrm{n}}}{\left(1+x^{2 \mathrm{~m}}\right)\left(1+y^{2 \mathrm{n}}\right)}$ is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $A=\frac{x^{m} y^{n}}{\left(1+x^{2 m}\right)\left(1+y^{2 n}\right)}=\frac{1}{\left(x^{-m}+x^{m}\right)\left(y^{-n}+y^{n}\right)}\frac{x^{m}+y^{-m}}{2} \geq\left(x^{n+1}, x^{-m}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} \Rightarrow x^{n+}+x^{-n} \geq 2$ In the same way, $y^{n}+y^{n} \geq 2$ Then $,\left(x^{n}+x^{-n}\right)\left(y^{-n}+y^{n}\right) \geq 4\Rightarrow \frac{1}{\left(x^{\text {"1 }}+x^{-m}\right)\left(y^{-n}+y^{n}\right)} \leq \frac{1}{4}$

questions.q: Let ${S}_{n}$ be the sum of the first $n$ terms of an arithmetic progression. If ${S}_{3n} = 3{S}_{2n}$, then the value of $\dfrac{S4n}{S2n}$ is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let $a$ be first term and $d$ be common difference~of this A.P.

Given ${S}_{3n} = 3{S}_{2n}$

$⇒ \dfrac{3n}{2} \left[2a + \left($3n - 1\right)d\right] = 3 $\times \dfrac{2n}{2}\left[$2a + \left($2n - 1\right)d\right]$

$⇒ 2a + ( 3n - 1 ) d = 4a + ( 4n - 2 ) d$

$⇒ 2a + ( n - 1 ) d = 0$

Now \dfrac{S4n}{S2n} = \dfrac{\dfrac{4n}{2}\left[2a + \left(4n - 1\right)d\right]}{\dfrac{2n}{2}\left[2a + \left(2n - 1\right)d\right]} =$2 \left[2a + \left($n - 1\right)d + 3nd\right]\left[2a + \left(n - 1\right)d + nd\right]$

$= \dfrac{6nd}{nd} =6$

$

questions.q: Let ${x}_{1}, {x}_{2}, \ldots , {x}_{100}$ be in an arithmetic progression, with ${x}_{1} = 2$~and their mean equal to $200$ . If ${y}_{i} = i\left({x}_{i} - i\right), 1 \le i \le 100$, then the mean of ${y}_{1}, {y}_{2}, \ldots$, ${y}_{100}$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$

Given,

Mean of& ${x}_{1}, {x}_{2} . . . . . . . . . . , {x}_{100}$~is~$200$

So, the sum of observation will be,

$∑ {x}_{i} = 100 \times 200$

Now using the sum of~$A . P$~formula in above equation as all terms are in arithmetic progression we get,

$\dfrac{100}{2}\left({x}_{1} + {x}_{100}\right) = 100 \times 200$

$⇒ 50\left(2 + {x}_{100}\right) = 100 \times 200$

$⇒ {x}_{100} = 398$

$⇒ {x}_{1} + 99d = 398$

$⇒ d = 4$

Now,~${x}_{i} = 2 + ( i - 1 ) 4 = 4i - 2$

So,~${y}_{i} = i\left({x}_{i} - i\right) = 3i^{2} - 2i$

Now finding mean we get,

$\overset{¯}{y} = \dfrac{1}{100} ∑ {y}_{i}$

$⇒ \overset{¯}{y} = \dfrac{1}{100} ∑ \left(3i^{2} - 2i\right)$

$⇒ \overset{¯}{y} = $\dfrac{1}{100} \left[3 \times $\dfrac{100 \times 101 \times 201}{6} -2\dfrac{100 \times 101}{2}\right]

$⇒ \overset{¯}{y} = $\$left[\dfrac{101 \times 201}{2} -$101\right]$

$⇒ \overset{¯}{y} = 10049 . 5$

$

questions.q: The number of $3$-digit numbers, that are divisible by either $2$ or $3$ but not divisible by $7$ is _____ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$We know that total number of three-digit number will be& $900$,

Now let~$n \left(A\right)$~be number of three-digit number which are divisible by~$2$, i.e,

$A = \left\{100, 102, . . . , 998\right\}$

$⇒ n\left(A\right) = 450$

$n\left(B\right)$~be number of three-digit number which are divisible by~$3$, i.e,~$B = \left\{102, 105, . . . , 999\right\}$

$n\left(B\right) = 300$

Numbers divisible by both~$2$~and~$3$~is

\left\{102, 108, . . . 996\right\}$~i.e,~$150$

Numbers divisible by both~$2$~and~$7$~are~\left\{112, 126, . . . , 994\right\}$~i.e.,~$64$~numbers.

Numbers divisible by both~$3$~and~$7$~is~\left\{105, 126, . . . 987\right\}$~i.e,~$43$~numbers.

Numbers divisible by~$2, 3 \text{ and } 7$~is~\left\{126, 168, . . . , 966\right\}$~i.e,~$21$~numbers.

Required number

$= 450 + 150 - 64 - 43 + 21 = 514$

Hence,~$514$~three-digit number are there which are divisible by~2\$ttext{or}3\text{but not divisible by}$7$.

questions.q: The value of& $0 . {16}^{\log_{2 . 5}\left(\dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{32} + \dfrac{1}{33} + \ldots . \infty\right)}$& is __________
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$0 . {16}^{\log_{2 . 5}\left(\dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{32} + \dfrac{1}{33} + \ldots . \infty\right)}$

$= 0 . {16}^{\log_{2 . 5} \left(\dfrac{\dfrac{1}{3}}{1 - \dfrac{1}{3}}\right)} = \left(\dfrac{4}{25}\rrright)log\dfrac{5}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)

$= \left(\dfrac{5}{2}\rrright)-2log\dfrac{5}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)-2 = 4$

$

questions.q: Consider an arithmetic series and a geometric series having four initial terms from the set& \left\{11, 8, 21, 16, 26, 32, 4\right\}$. If the last terms of these series are the maximum possible four digit numbers, then the number of common terms in these two series is equal to _______.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given set$= \left\{11, 8, 21, 16, 26, 32, 4\right\}$

Given an arithmetic series and a geometric series having the first four terms from the given set.~

Then,~

$\text{Geometric series}: 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192$

$\text{Arithmetic series}: 11, 16, 21, 26, 31, 36, . . . , 256, . . . . 4096, . . .$

${T}_{n} ( G . P . ) = 4 \cdot {2}^{n - 1}$

${T}_{n} ( A . P . ) = 11 + 5\left(n - 1\right) = 5n + 6$

For common terms,~$4 \cdot {2}^{n - 1} = 5n + 6$

So, common terms are~$16, 256, 4096$ only.

questions.q: If $m$ arithmetic means (A.Ms) and three geometric means (G.Ms) are inserted between~$3$~and $243$ such that ${4}^{th}$ A.M. is equal to ${2}^{nd}$~G.M., then $m$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let& $3, {A}_{1}, {A}_{2}, {A}_{3}, . . . . . . {A}_{m}, 243$~are in arithmetic progression with~$m$~arithmetic means.

Common difference~$d = \dfrac{243 - 3}{m + 1} = \dfrac{240}{m + 1}$

Let~$3, {G}_{1}, {G}_{2}, {G}_{3}, 243$~are in geometric progression with~$3$ geometric means.

Common ratio~$r = \left(\dfrac{243}{3}\right)\dfrac{1}{3 + 1} = \left(81\right)\dfrac{1}{4} = 3$

Given~${G}_{2} = {A}_{4}$

$⇒ 3 \left(3\right)2 = 3 + 4 \left(\dfrac{240}{m + 1}\right)

$⇒ 27 = 3 + $\dfrac{960}{m + 1}

$⇒ m + 1 = 40$

$⇒ m = 39$

$

questions.q: If three successive terms of a G.P. with common ratio $r  \left(r > 1\right)$ are the length of the sides of a triangle and  \left[r\right]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to r, then $3 \left[r\right] +  \left[-$r\right] is equal to:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Let, $a, ar, ar^{2} \to G . P .$

It is given that sum of any two sides is greater than the third side.

$⇒ a + ar > ar^{2}, a + ar^{2} > ar, ar + ar^{2} > a$

Case-I: $r^{2} - r - 1 < 0$

$⇒ r = \dfrac{1 \pm \sqrt{1 - 4 \times 1 \times \left(- 1\right)}}{2}$

$⇒ r = \dfrac{1 \pm \sqrt{5}}{2}$

$⇒ r \in \left(\dfrac{1 - \sqrt{5}}{2}, \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}\right) . . .\left($i\right)$

Case-II: $r^{2} - r + 1 > 0$ is always true.

Case-III: $r^{2} + r - 1 > 0$

$⇒ r \in \left(- \infty, \dfrac{- 1 - \sqrt{5}}{2}\right)∪ $\$left(\dfrac{- 1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}, \infty\right) . . . \left($ii\right)$

Taking intersection of \left(i\$right)\text{and}\left($ii\right)$

$⇒ r \in $\$left(\dfrac{- 1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}, \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}\right)

As $r > 1$

$⇒ r \in \left($1, \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{2}\right)$

$⇒ \left[$r\right] = 1$\text{and}\left[-$r\right] = - 2$

$⇒ 3\left[$r\right] + \left[-$r\right] = 3 - 2$

$⇒ 3\left[$r\right] + \left[-$r\right] = 1$

$
